content.p: Baba Siddique, a veteran Mumbai politician known as much for his Bollywood iftar parties as for his years as a minister, was shot outside his son's office in the Bandra area on the night of 12 October 2024. He was 66. The killing, in a crowded street during Dussehra celebrations and weeks before state elections, was, in the BBC's words, the first major assassination of a politician in the city since the 1990s.

Police told a court that Anmol Bishnoi, the younger brother of the jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi, emerged as the main conspirator, and 27 arrested people have been charge-sheeted. Everyone named is accused and presumed innocent. On 10 February 2026 a special court framed charges against the 27, all of whom pleaded not guilty; the Tribune describes the framing of charges as the first stage of a criminal trial. The man the police call the main conspirator, Anmol Bishnoi, is listed in the charge sheet as a wanted accused.

The BBC reported that Siddique was born in Bihar and was brought to Mumbai at the age of five by his father, a watchmaker. He began as a student leader in the Congress party, then led its youth wing in the city, sat in the local council and won election to the state legislature three times in a row. He became a state minister in 2004 and served for about four years. In February 2024 he left Congress and joined the NCP, a partner in the governing coalition.

His iftar parties during Ramadan drew Bollywood stars. At his 2013 event, the BBC noted, Salman Khan and Shah Rukh Khan ended a well-publicised rift with a hug. Siddique was also thought to have received a death threat about two weeks before his killing, local media reported, and his security was upgraded days earlier.

Siddique was leaving his son Zeeshan's office when three men opened fire between about 9:15 and 9:30 p.m., according to Mumbai police quoted by The Tribune. Police said six rounds were fired and two struck him in the chest. The BBC reported six or seven rounds and said a bystander was hit in the leg by a stray bullet. The gunmen took cover in the noise of Dussehra fireworks, police said, and many people in the congested area thought they were hearing firecrackers.

Three constables were assigned to him under non-categorised security, which is given according to a person's perceived level of threat, but two had been relieved earlier that evening, so one was with him. He was taken to Lilavati Hospital and declared dead. A police officer from Nirmal Nagar station and other personnel rushed to the spot and detained two of the alleged shooters, recovering pistols and live rounds. The third escaped in the crowd. Opposition parties accused the government of a serious security lapse; Maharashtra's chief minister, Eknath Shinde, said the culprits would not be spared "be it the Bishnoi gang or any underworld gang".

Outlook reported that the two detained were Gurmail Baljit Singh, 23, and Dharmaraj Rajesh Kashyap, 19, and that the third suspected shooter, Shivkumar Gautam of Uttar Pradesh, had fled. Police arrested Pravin Lonkar, whose lawyer says he runs a dairy shop and whom police accuse of hiring two of the shooters; his lawyer said his client was being made a "scapegoat" because police could not find his brother, Shubham Lonkar. A fourth arrest, of Harishkumar Balakram, followed on 15 October. Police said the plan was hatched in Pune, that the shooters were shown a photograph of Siddique, and that they carried out reconnaissance of his routine. Fifteen police teams worked in several states.

By 30 November Mumbai police had arrested 26 people and invoked MCOCA, a law under which confessions made to police are admissible and bail is hard to obtain, Deccan Herald noted. Defence lawyers opposing remand argued that the law did not apply because the accused had no previous cases and nothing showed they belonged to a gang with two earlier charge sheets.

Within hours of the shooting, a Facebook post circulated in the name of an alleged Lawrence Bishnoi gang member claiming responsibility. Police said they were verifying it. Outlook later reported that the post was by Shubham Lonkar, who police say is linked to the gang, and had been deleted but was widely screenshotted; The Tribune also described him as a suspected gang member who claimed responsibility. The BBC noted on 15 October that police had not yet confirmed the post's authenticity. Lawrence Bishnoi has been in jail since 2015, and the BBC noted that it was unclear how he directed the gang's operations from prison. Investigators told a court earlier that the role of Lawrence Bishnoi had not been established, according to The Tribune, and that his brother Anmol was operating a separate gang, mainly active in Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh.

The Crime Branch filed a 4,590-page charge sheet on 6 January 2025 in the special MCOCA court after 85 days of investigation, naming 26 arrested people and three wanted ones: Anmol Bishnoi, Shubham Lonkar and a man named as Zeeshan Akhtar, who is called Mohammad Yasin Akhtar in another report. Investigators listed 180 witnesses, and seized five weapons, six magazines and 35 mobile phones, among other items.

The prosecution alleges that Anmol Bishnoi ordered the killing to create an atmosphere of terror and show the dominance of his crime syndicate. It alleges the gang paid a contract of 17 lakh rupees, sent from several bank accounts, and identifies three motives: Siddique's closeness to the actor Salman Khan and to the underworld figure Dawood Ibrahim, his suspected involvement in the death of Anuj Thapan, who was accused in the firing at Salman Khan's home, and the gang's wish to establish itself in Mumbai's underworld. The charge sheet says the plan began after the firing at Salman Khan's residence on 14 April 2024; the gang first considered Salman Khan, then switched to Siddique because of Khan's tight security. It claims an earlier attempt during the Ganpati immersion failed because of the crowd, and that the gang had also planned to kill Zeeshan Siddique, who was absent. These are the prosecution's allegations and have not been tested at trial.

Anmol Bishnoi was detained in the United States in November 2024. He was deported to India on 19 November 2025 and was sent by a Delhi court to National Investigation Agency custody for 11 days in connection with a separate terrorism-syndicate case. The agency said it was investigating his role in the gang's activities. According to officials he faces at least 18 criminal cases in India, including the conspiracy to murder Siddique, the firing at Salman Khan's home and the 2022 killing of the singer Sidhu Moosewala. Zeeshan Siddique said the family had been told of Anmol's removal from the United States and called him a "threat to society". In the February 2026 report of the framing of charges, the Mumbai charge sheet still showed Anmol as a wanted accused in the Siddique case.

On 10 February 2026 special judge Satyanarayan R Navander framed charges against the 27 charge-sheeted accused under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for murder, under MCOCA, under the Arms Act and under the Maharashtra Police Act. All pleaded not guilty. No verdict has been reported, and the prosecution's allegations have not been tested at trial.
